## Bentham

*An Introduction to the Principles of Morals and Legislation*, printed 1780, published 1789. "Nature has placed mankind under the governance of two sovereign masters, pain and pleasure." The felicific calculus measures a pleasure by seven circumstances: intensity, duration, certainty, propinquity, fecundity, purity and extent. I make students try to score a Friday night out on all seven. Nobody can agree on propinquity.

Saw the auto-icon at UCL in May 2023: Bentham's skeleton, dressed in his own clothes, with a wax head. The real head was kept separately after students stole it, reputedly in 1975.

## Mill

*Utilitarianism*, serialised in *Fraser's Magazine* in 1861, as a book in 1863. The higher and lower pleasures: "It is better to be a human being dissatisfied than a pig satisfied; better to be Socrates dissatisfied than a fool satisfied" (Hackett edition, p. 10). Critics say this smuggles in a non-hedonist value. I agree with them and I still quote it every year.

## Act versus rule

Act utilitarianism judges each act by its outcome. Rule utilitarianism judges rules by the outcome of everyone following them. The surgeon case is the standard test: five patients each need an organ, one healthy visitor in the waiting room. The act utilitarian sums say operate; the rule version says a world where hospitals do that is a world where nobody visits hospitals. Compare the lever and the footbridge in [[Trolley problem]]: same five against one, but here the class is unanimous against.

## Objections I find hardest

- Bernard Williams, "Jim and Pedro", in Smart and Williams, *Utilitarianism: For and Against* (1973), p. 98. Shoot one villager and Pedro spares the other nineteen. The point is not that Jim should refuse but that the theory makes Jim's integrity irrelevant.
- Derek Parfit, *Reasons and Persons* (1984), p. 388: the repugnant conclusion. A huge population of lives barely worth living could add up to more total good than ten billion flourishing ones.
- Nozick's experience machine (1974), which my sixth years love.

## Where it leads

Peter Singer's 1972 drowning child argument comes straight out of this, and so does most of [[Effective altruism]]. Also the background for a lot of what gets said about [[Ethics of AI]] when people talk about "maximising" anything.
